---
title: "Study A — Did host gene expression change with treatment?"
date: 2026-11-12
format: html
---

## The question

The last document looked at the *bacteria*. This one looks at the *host*:
did the expression of vaginal epithelial genes change from pre to post, and
did the probiotic arm change differently from the placebo arm?

This is the week's set-piece: the gene count table is exactly the same shape
as the species table, so the microViz pipeline — written for bacteria — runs
on human genes unchanged. We use it for the transcriptome-wide view, and
DESeq2 for the per-gene view.

Two sub-questions again:

1. **Did gene expression change at all?** — both overall (is the
   transcriptome at post different from pre?) and gene by gene.
2. **Differently by arm?** — did the probiotic arm's genes change more, or
   in different genes, than the placebo arm's?

Two workshop rules we follow strictly. **Raw counts go into DESeq2** — never
CPM, never logged; it does its own normalisation. And **the column order of
the count matrix must match the row order of the sample table** — DESeq2
will not warn you, it will just be wrong, so we assert it.

## Setup and QC rules

Same population as the community document: participant A116 is dropped
(both visits), giving 175 participants × 2 visits = 350 samples. Honest
note: A116's *RNA-seq* is actually fine (10.7M and 12.6M reads) — the QC rule
was about its failed microbiome sample. We keep the same people here so the
two documents describe the same population, and list the alternative in
`Choices made`.

```{r setup}
#| message: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(microViz); library(phyloseq)})

source(here::here("R/count_tables.R"))
d  <- read_counts("group_a")
md <- d$metadata
g  <- d$genes

keep_samples <- md$sample_id[md$participant_id != "A116"]   # 175 x 2 = 350
```

## 1. Transcriptome-wide: how far did each person's expression move?

**Aitchison distance** is the standard distance for compositional count
data: each sample's genes are log-transformed and recentred on that
sample's own average, which turns counts into log-*ratios* — a gene
doubling is the same change whether the library is big or small, and one
very abundant gene no longer drowns out the rest. microViz computes it
straight from raw counts (`dist_calc("aitchison")`).

```{r gene-pcoa}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-path: figures/
ps  <- prune_samples(keep_samples, as_counts("group_a", "rnaseq"))
# same prevalence rule as the community document: a gene must have
# at least 10 counts in at least 10% of samples to enter.
psf <- tax_filter(ps, min_prevalence = 0.1, prev_detection_threshold = 10)
ntaxa(psf); nsamples(psf)     # 14217 genes, 350 samples

ord <- psf |>
  dist_calc("aitchison") |>   # Aitchison = Euclidean on log-ratioed genes
  ord_calc("PCoA")
ord_plot(ord,
  colour = "time_point", alt_colour = "steelblue",
  shape  = "arm",
  alpha  = 0.7
) + theme_minimal()
```

```{r gene-shift}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-path: figures/
dm <- as.matrix(ord@dist)     # the full sample-to-sample distance matrix

gp <- data.frame(sample_data(psf))
pairs <- gp |>
  select(participant_id, arm, time_point) |>
  mutate(sample_id = rownames(gp)) |>
  select(participant_id, arm, time_point, sample_id) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = time_point, values_from = sample_id) |>
  mutate(shift = dm[cbind(pre, post)])   # own-pre-to-own-post distance

ggplot(pairs, aes(arm, shift, fill = arm)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Aitchison distance, pre to post",
       title = "Within-participant expression shift, by arm") +
  theme_minimal()

wilcox.test(shift ~ arm, data = pairs)
median(pairs$shift[pairs$arm == "probiotic"])
median(pairs$shift[pairs$arm == "placebo"])
```

**What we see:** every participant's expression profile moved, but the two
arms moved the **same amount** — median Aitchison shift 71.9 (probiotic) vs
70.9 (placebo), Wilcoxon p = 0.55. Nothing like the community result, where
the probiotic arm's bacteria moved further. (For scale, these Aitchison
numbers are on a log-ratio scale, not 0–1 like Bray-Curtis.)

Is there any overall pre→post signal at all in the genes? PERMANOVA, run
per arm with permutations restricted within participants, exactly as in
the community document:

```{r gene-permanova}
res_perm <- list()
for (a in c("probiotic", "placebo")) {
  smp  <- as.character(sample_names(psf))[gp$arm == a]
  ps_a <- prune_samples(smp, psf)
  sd_a <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_a))     # rows follow ps_a's sample order
  res_perm[[a]] <- ps_a |>
    dist_calc("aitchison") |>
    dist_permanova(variables = "time_point",
                   strata = sd_a$participant_id,   # permute within people
                   n_perms = 999)
}
permanova_row <- function(res, arm) {
  tab <- as.data.frame(res@permanova)
  tibble(arm = arm, R2 = tab$R2[1], F = tab$F[1], p = tab$`Pr(>F)`[1])
}
bind_rows(
  permanova_row(res_perm$probiotic, "probiotic"),
  permanova_row(res_perm$placebo,   "placebo")
) |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("arm", "R² (time_point)", "F", "permutation p"))
```

Yes, but small: `time_point` explains 0.7% of gene-expression variation in
the probiotic arm (p = 0.001) and 1.0% in the placebo arm (p = 0.016). Most
variation in expression is between people, and whatever changes with
treatment is a small, coordinated part of the transcriptome. The next
section finds out which part.

## 2. Which genes changed? DESeq2, per arm

We fit DESeq2 separately in each arm with the paired design
`~ participant + time`. Each participant appears twice, so the model asks:
**what changed within the same people from pre to post?** Library-size
differences between samples are handled by DESeq2's size factors, and the
`participant` term means a person who simply runs "high" on everything does
not distort the pre/post comparison.

One design check first: every participant's two samples were sequenced in
the same RNA-seq batch (`rnaseq_batch` is constant within person), so batch
is already absorbed by the `participant` term and does not need its own
column.

```{r deseq2}
#| cache: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# Warning: this chunk takes roughly 30 minutes the FIRST time it runs
# (175 participant columns make a big model). knitr caches it, so later
# re-renders skip it unless this code changes.
library(DESeq2)

mdk <- md |> filter(sample_id %in% keep_samples) |> as.data.frame()
rownames(mdk) <- mdk$sample_id
gk  <- g[, keep_samples]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(gk), rownames(mdk)))   # THE order check
gk  <- gk[rowSums(gk >= 10) >= 35, ]                # same filter as above: 14217

run_arm <- function(a) {
  cd <- mdk[mdk$arm == a, ]            # rows = samples, in matrix column order
  m  <- gk[, rownames(cd)]
  cd$participant <- factor(cd$participant_id)
  cd$time <- relevel(factor(cd$time_point), "pre")   # 'pre' is the reference
  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(m, cd, design = ~ participant + time)
  dds <- DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)
  list(dds = dds, res = results(dds, contrast = c("time", "post", "pre")))
}
res_all <- list()
for (a in c("probiotic", "placebo")) res_all[[a]] <- run_arm(a)
```

```{r deseq2-counts}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-path: figures/
de_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(res_all), function(a) {
  r <- as.data.frame(res_all[[a]]$res)
  tibble(arm = a,
         `significant (padj<0.05)` = sum(r$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
         `  of which |LFC| > 0.5` = sum(r$padj < 0.05 & abs(r$log2FoldChange) > 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
         up  = sum(r$padj < 0.05 & r$log2FoldChange > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
         down = sum(r$padj < 0.05 & r$log2FoldChange < 0, na.rm = TRUE))
})) |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), as.integer))
knitr::kable(de_summary)

de_summary |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(up, down), names_to = "direction", values_to = "n") |>
  ggplot(aes(arm, n, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "number of genes (padj < 0.05)",
       title = "Expression changes at one month: more genes move in the probiotic arm") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**What we see:** expression changed in **both arms**, but more genes cleared
the significance bar in the probiotic arm: **812 genes** there (390 up, 422
down) versus **233** in placebo (92 up, 141 down). Most of these are
*modest* changes — only 78 (probiotic) and 35 (placebo) also have a
log2 fold-change above 0.5, i.e. a 40% change or more. `padj` is the
adjusted p-value: the false-discovery-rate-corrected version that accounts
for running the test 14,217 times.

The strongest hits, ranked by padj:

```{r deseq2-top}
sym <- d$gene_info |> mutate(symbol = coalesce(symbol, ensembl_gene_id))
top_tab <- function(res, n = 10) {
  df <- as.data.frame(res) |> arrange(padj) |> head(n)
  tibble(gene      = sym$symbol[match(rownames(df), sym$ensembl_gene_id)],
         `gene name` = sym$gene_name[match(rownames(df), sym$ensembl_gene_id)],
         baseMean  = round(df$baseMean),
         log2FC    = round(df$log2FoldChange, 2),
         padj      = signif(df$padj, 2))
}
knitr::kable(top_tab(res_all$probiotic$res),
             caption = "Probiotic arm: top genes, pre to post")
knitr::kable(top_tab(res_all$placebo$res),
             caption = "Placebo arm: top genes, pre to post")
```

The flavour of the two lists is different. The probiotic arm's strongest
changes are *down-regulations* of mucosal/epithelial genes (DMBT1, FCGBP,
SLC26A4, SLC9A3, TFPI). The placebo arm's are *up-regulations* of
interferon-response and chemokine genes — **CXCL10** (+0.94), **CXCL11**
(+1.35), **OAS2** — the classic "antiviral alarm" programme. Before making
anything of that, we test the arm difference formally.

## 3. Did the arms change differently?

Two views: which genes were significant where, and a formal per-gene test
of "changed differently in probiotic vs placebo".

```{r overlap}
sig_p <- rownames(as.data.frame(res_all$probiotic$res))[which(res_all$probiotic$res$padj < 0.05)]
sig_l <- rownames(as.data.frame(res_all$placebo$res))[which(res_all$placebo$res$padj < 0.05)]
c(both = sum(sig_p %in% sig_l),
  probiotic_only = sum(!sig_p %in% sig_l),
  placebo_only   = sum(!sig_l %in% sig_p))

# the shared genes: same direction, or opposite?
rp <- res_all$probiotic$res[sig_p %in% sig_l, ]
rl <- res_all$placebo$res[sig_p %in% sig_l, ]
sum(sign(rp$log2FoldChange) == sign(rl$log2FoldChange))   # of 37
```

Of the probiotic arm's 812 hits, only **37 are also hits in placebo** — and
all 37 change in the *same direction*. So the bulk of the pre→post response
is arm-specific in *significance*, though both arms do show some shared
signal.

For a formal arm contrast per gene: compare the two arms' log fold-changes.
The two arms contain different people, so the two LFCs are independent
estimates, and a **z test** of their difference — the difference divided by
its combined uncertainty — is the interaction test ("did the change depend
on the arm?"). We correct across genes as before.

```{r interaction}
cmn <- intersect(rownames(res_all$probiotic$res), rownames(res_all$placebo$res))
rp <- res_all$probiotic$res[cmn, ]
rl <- res_all$placebo$res[cmn, ]
z  <- (rp$log2FoldChange - rl$log2FoldChange) / sqrt(rp$lfcSE^2 + rl$lfcSE^2)
padj_int <- p.adjust(2 * pnorm(-abs(z)), "BH")

c(sig_padj05 = sum(padj_int < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
  sig_padj01 = sum(padj_int < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE))

int_tab <- tibble(
  ensembl = cmn[order(padj_int)][1:10],
  gene = sym$symbol[cmn[order(padj_int)][1:10]],
  `LFC probiotic` = round(rp$log2FoldChange[order(padj_int)][1:10], 2),
  `LFC placebo`   = round(rl$log2FoldChange[order(padj_int)][1:10], 2),
  padj = signif(padj_int[order(padj_int)][1:10], 2))
knitr::kable(int_tab, caption = "Genes whose pre→post change differs most between arms")
```

Only **5 genes** pass the arm-contrast test at padj < 0.05, and **none**
at padj < 0.01. But look at the top of that list: CXCL10, OAS2, STAT1,
then MX1 and PARP14 just below the cut — the interferon-response programme
again, this time saying it went **up in placebo and flat in probiotic**.
Here is the strongest one, in everyone's raw-normalised counts:

```{r cxcl10}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-path: figures/
gene_id <- sym$ensembl_gene_id[sym$symbol == "CXCL10"]
pc <- rbind(
  transform(plotCounts(res_all$probiotic$dds, gene_id, intgroup = "time_point",
                      returnData = TRUE), arm = "probiotic"),
  transform(plotCounts(res_all$placebo$dds,  gene_id, intgroup = "time_point",
                      returnData = TRUE), arm = "placebo")
)
ggplot(pc, aes(time_point, count, colour = time_point)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ arm) +
  labs(title = "CXCL10, normalised counts (log scale), pre vs post",
       subtitle = "Rises in placebo; stays flat in probiotic") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Answer, and what we do not claim

**Did host gene expression change from pre to post? Yes, in both arms.**
The transcriptome-wide test is significant in both arms (though the effect
is small: R² = 0.7–1.0%), and hundreds of individual genes change in each
arm — 812 in the probiotic arm, 233 in placebo, mostly small changes.

**Differently by arm? In amount, no; in which genes, mostly yes; in
direction, only barely.**

- The *size* of the within-person expression shift is identical in the two
  arms (Aitchison 71.9 vs 70.9, p = 0.55) — unlike the bacteria, where the
  probiotic arm moved further.
- The *significant-gene lists* barely overlap (37 genes shared of 812/233),
  but significance is partly a power artefact: the probiotic arm is bigger
  (120 vs 55 participants), so it detects smaller changes.
- The *formal arm contrast* finds only 5 genes, of which the interpretable
  pattern is an interferon-response programme (CXCL10, OAS2, STAT1) that
  **rose in placebo and not in probiotic**. We present this as *suggestive,
  not established*: nothing survives padj < 0.01, we tested 14,217 genes,
  and we have no untreated control to say what the placebo arm would have
  done anyway.

Two claims we deliberately do not make. We do not say any gene "went up"
in absolute terms: like the species table, the gene table is **compositional**
— RNA-seq measures each gene's share of a fixed-size library, so a log
fold-change means "a larger share of the sample's output". And we do not
yet connect the host response to the bacterial shift or to symptoms — that
is the multi-omics integration the workshop has been building towards.

## Check it yourself

- **The order check:** shuffle it and watch it stop —
  `colnames(gk) <- sample(colnames(gk))` before the `stopifnot` line
  crashes the chunk. This is the bug the workshop warns about, caught.
- **The DE counts:** `sum(res_all$probiotic$res$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)`
  should be 812, placebo 233. If your filter changed (`rowSums(gk >= 10) >= 35`),
  your numbers will differ from ours — that is the point of listing it.
- **A top gene:** recompute DMBT1's direction by eye —
  `plotCounts(res_all$probiotic$dds, "ENSG00000187908", intgroup = "time_point")`.
  The post points should sit lower than pre.
- **The interaction:** redo CXCL10's z by hand from the two results
  tables: LFCs −0.24 (probiotic) and +0.94 (placebo), standard errors in
  `lfcSE`. You should get padj ≈ 0.026.
- **The runtime claim:** time the DESeq2 chunk on a re-render — with the
  cache warm it should be seconds, not minutes.

## Choices made

- **Same 175 participants as the community document (A116 dropped)** —
  alternative: keep A116 here, since its RNA-seq is healthy (10.7M/12.6M
  reads), giving 176 participants; we chose the shared population so the
  two documents describe the same people.
- **Gene filter: ≥10 counts in ≥10% of samples (14,217 of 14,226)** —
  alternative: no filter; zeros distort the Aitchison distance, though for
  host RNA-seq (expressed nearly everywhere) it barely bites either way.
- **Aitchison distance via microViz's built-in `dist_calc("aitchison")`** —
  alternative: Bray-Curtis on compositional data (dominated by the most
  abundant genes) or robust Aitchison (ignores genes absent in either of a
  compared pair).
- **PERMANOVA per arm with `strata = participant_id`, 999 permutations** —
  alternative: one pooled PERMANOVA ignoring the pairing, which inflates
  significance.
- **DESeq2 on raw counts, fit separately per arm, design
  `~ participant + time`** — alternative: one combined model with a
  time×arm interaction term, equivalent information at the cost of a
  bigger fit.
- **Arm contrast by z test on the two arms' LFCs, BH-corrected** —
  alternative: the formal DESeq2 interaction coefficient; the z test uses
  the same estimates and is instant, at the cost of the approximation.
- **Batch left out of the design** (verified: both visits of every
  participant are in the same RNA-seq batch, so `participant` absorbs it) —
  alternative: an explicit `rnaseq_batch` column, unidentifiable next to
  `participant`.
- **Significance called at padj < 0.05 (BH), also reporting padj < 0.01
  and |LFC| > 0.5** — alternative: a single threshold, which would have
  hidden how modest most fold-changes are.
- **Top genes ranked by padj, unshrunk LFCs** — alternative: shrunken LFCs
  (`lfcShrink`), which are more stable but slower and less familiar.
- **Cached the DESeq2 chunk (first render ≈ 30 minutes)** — alternative:
  no cache and a painful re-render every edit.
